name: Oil & Exploration
scope: Upstream oil & gas: global prices, supply and forecasts, India's output, gas pricing, levies and exploration policy, and what they mean for Indian listed producers, service and equipment firms, the gas chain and refiners.

summary.one_line: Brent is holding near $104 with Hormuz flows still about 30% below normal, the EIA has raised its forecasts by $5-14/bbl, OPEC+ has paused its quota increases, and India has raised the deepwater gas ceiling to $9.89 while legacy APM gas stays capped at $7 (S2; S1; S5; S6).
key_points: Brent futures settled at $104.47/bbl on 9 October after a 4% jump to $104.28 on 8 October, when Iran stepped up attacks on Hormuz tankers; Kpler counts about 9.5 mb/d leaving Hormuz, about 30% below pre-war levels (S2).

The EIA's October STEO (6 October) raised its 4Q26 Brent forecast to $104.69 from $90.66, 2026 to $96.32 from $91.01 and 2027 to $83.74 from $73.74, but still expects prices to fall from early-October levels (S1).
The EIA estimates global stocks fell 1.9 mb/d in 3Q26 and will fall another 0.7 mb/d in 4Q26; it puts closure-related shut-ins at 4.8 mb/d in September, down from a 10.9 mb/d peak in May (S1).
Seven core OPEC+ members on 4 October held November required output at September levels (31.01 mb/d combined) after four monthly increases of 188 kb/d; they meet next on 1 November (S5).
India raised the deepwater/HPHT gas price ceiling to $9.89/MMBtu for October 2026-March 2027 from $8.90; legacy APM gas stays capped at $7.00 although the formula price for October is $11.22 (S6).
The export duty (SAED) fell from 1 October to ₹16/litre on diesel (from ₹20) and ₹10.5 on ATF (from ₹15); petrol stays at ₹0.5 (S7).

India imported 5.251 mb/d of crude in 1-27 September (+13% on August); Russia supplied 1.742 mb/d, its lowest since April, while US law now allows tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian energy (S8).
ONGC's Mahanadi deepwater find tested close to 2.25 MMSCMD and testing is still under way; deepwater bids under OALP-X/XI close on 15 November (S11; S10).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Producers with Brent-linked crude: ONGC realised $99.45/bbl on nomination crude in Q1 FY27 and Oil India $98.73/bbl, with Brent still above $100 in October (S12; S13; S2).
Deepwater gas producers: the $9.89 ceiling applies to Reliance-BP's KG-D6, whose Q1 gas realisation was $8.89 (S6; S14).

Offshore contractors and rig owners: L&T won a ₹2,500-5,000 cr ONGC offshore platform order, Transocean a $300 mn ONGC drillship award, and Jindal Drilling a three-year ONGC rig contract (S16; S17; S11).
Line-pipe makers: Welspun Corp's order book is a record $4.7 bn after a $412.5 mn US order (S18).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Oil marketing companies: HPCL, BPCL and IOC all posted Q1 FY27 losses, and Emkay has cut its full-year outlook because crude rose again (S25; S26).
Legacy gas: the APM cap of $7 is $4.22 below the October formula price, so ONGC and Oil India keep none of the upside on old fields (S6).
LNG importers: Qatar's force majeure has hit 56 Petronet cargoes, and GAIL's marketing volumes fell to 93.82 MMSCMD in Q1 (S24; S23).
Refiners using Russian barrels face possible US tariffs; ICRA says replacing about 2 mb/d of Russian crude would be difficult (S8).
Declining private output: Vedanta Oil & Gas's Q1 gross production fell 17% to 77.7 kboepd and KG-D6 gas fell 7% to 24.8 MMSCMD (S15; S14).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: US-Iran talks and Hormuz tanker flows; President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before next month's midterm elections (S2).
OPEC+ meeting on 1 November and its delayed capacity review for 2027 baselines (S5).
Fortnightly SAED revisions, next due around mid-October (S7).
Mahanadi flow-test results and Samudra Manthan rules ahead of the 15 November deepwater bid deadline (S11; S10).
Q2 FY27 results: brokers expect OMC margins to recover sharply from Q1 (S26).

sections.title: The theme: a long Gulf disruption, higher forecasts and a shrinking Indian output base

blocks.text: Prices are back above $100. Brent futures rose 4% to settle at $104.28 on 8 October as Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and a hurricane threatened US Gulf of Mexico output, then settled at $104.47 on 9 October after President Trump called talks 'productive' and said the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections (S2). Kpler data show about 9.5 mb/d leaving Hormuz in the week to 6 October, about 30% below pre-war levels (S2).

Measures of lost supply differ by source. The EIA puts closure-related shut-ins at 4.8 mb/d in September, down from 5.8 mb/d in August and a 10.9 mb/d peak in May, and assumes 4.5 mb/d in 4Q26 and 2.7 mb/d in 1Q27 (S1). The IEA's September report, the latest available, said more than 10 mb/d of Gulf output was still shut in during August and that observed stocks had fallen 507 mb since February (S3). The EIA estimates global stocks fell 1.9 mb/d in 3Q26 and expects a further 0.7 mb/d draw in 4Q26 (S1).

OPEC+ has stopped adding barrels on paper. On 4 October Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman kept November required production at September levels, 31.01 mb/d combined, after four monthly increases of 188 kb/d from June to September; they meet again on 1 November (S5).

subsections.title: India: falling output, high import dependence

blocks.text: India's crude output fell about 3% in FY26, the third straight annual decline; ONGC held its own decline to about 2% through enhanced and improved recovery, and India imports as much as 90% of its crude (S9). It imports about half of its gas (S11).

Crude imports rose to 5.251 mb/d in 1-27 September from 4.654 mb/d in August, per Kpler. Russia supplied 1.742 mb/d, the lowest since April, followed by Iraq (579 kb/d), Saudi Arabia (570 kb/d), the UAE (483 kb/d) and Kuwait (333 kb/d) (S8). A new US sanctions law could lead to tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian energy, including India (S8).

items: Samudra Manthan, the ₹84,084 cr National Offshore Exploration Scheme approved in late July, would cover up to 50% of deep and ultra-deep well costs, but its implementation rules are still pending (S10). Oil India cites a reimbursement ceiling of ₹675 cr per well and ₹10,000 cr for common infrastructure (S13).

Deepwater and ultra-deepwater bidding in OALP-X (25 blocks, 13 deep/ultra-deep) and OALP-XI (21 blocks, 5 deep/ultra-deep) now closes on 15 November 2026 after repeated extensions; OALP-X has been extended six times (S10).
ONGC's first Samudra Manthan well in the Mahanadi, about 43 km off Konark at around 1,600 m, has tested close to 2.25 MMSCMD of gas; testing is still under way (S11).
Deepwater exploration wells cost about $125-150 mn each, which is why the cost support matters (S9).

blocks.text: The EIA's October upgrade is the biggest forecast change this week: 4Q26 Brent up $14.03 to $104.69 and every 2027 quarter up $10, though its path still falls to $73.94 by 4Q27 as shut-ins ease (S1). The IEA (September) expects 2026 demand to shrink by 2.5 mb/d and supply to rebound 8 mb/d in 2027, while OPEC still sees 2026 demand growth (S3; S4).

items: Peace risk for producers: the EIA expects Brent to slide to $73.94 by 4Q27 as Middle East shut-ins fall (S1).
Escalation risk for refiners and gas users: tanker attacks pushed Brent up 4% in a day on 8 October (S2).
US tariffs on buyers of Russian energy could force costlier crude sourcing (S8).
Gas policy: the APM cap holds legacy realisations at $7 against an $11.22 formula price (S6).
Exploration risk: the Mahanadi well is still under test and deepwater bid rounds keep slipping (S11; S10).
Execution: Deep Industries' ONGC contract has already slipped 5-6 months (S19).

companies.name: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation
companies.role: India's largest crude and gas producer; Q1 FY27 output 4.452 MMT crude and 4.756 BCM gas (S12).
companies.impact: Brent above $100 supports crude realisations ($99.45/bbl in Q1), but legacy gas stays capped at $7 against an $11.22 formula; the Mahanadi find is still under test (S2; S6; S11; S12).

companies.name: Oil India
companies.role: State E&P with onshore and frontier assets that owns the Numaligarh refinery (S13).
companies.impact: Crude output grew 11% in Q1 and it plans 100 wells in FY27; high crude helps both upstream and NRL, while the APM cap limits gas upside (S6; S13).

companies.name: Reliance Industries
companies.role: Operator of the KG-D6 deepwater block (66.67%, with BP); Q1 gas 24.8 MMSCMD (S14).
companies.impact: The deepwater ceiling rises to $9.89 from October against an $8.89 Q1 realisation, partly offsetting a 7% volume decline (S6; S14).

companies.name: Vedanta Oil & Gas
companies.role: Private E&P anchored by Rajasthan, with Ravva and Cambay; 77.7 kboepd gross in Q1 FY27 (S15).
companies.impact: High crude prices help, but gross output fell 17% YoY and the Cambay block is tied up in a PSC-extension dispute (S15).

companies.role: Small E&P holding 100% of the D-11 Mahanadi offshore block with six gas discoveries (S11).

method: Week-41 refresh of the 2026-W40 edition, researched on 10 October 2026 with web search and page fetches. New this week: the EIA October STEO (via Ship & Bunker; the EIA PDF could not be parsed), Brent's move back above $104 and Kpler Hormuz flows (CNBC, from search results because the page blocked fetching), the 4 October OPEC+ decision, the October APM price and the October 2026-March 2027 deepwater/HPHT ceiling, the 1 October SAED cut, September crude imports by origin, L&T's ONGC offshore order, the Transocean ONGC drillship award, KG-D6 and Vedanta Oil & Gas Q1 output, GAIL Q1 results, the CGD APM incentive and Emkay's OMC preview. We re-opened carried-over sources (IEA September report via World Oil, IEF comparison, ONGC, Oil India, Deep Industries, Maharashtra Seamless and Welspun figures, OALP deadline, Mahanadi find). Dropped as stale or not re-confirmable: the September bank forecasts (HSBC, Goldman, BofA, Commerzbank), the FY26 crude output figure of 27.96 MMT (only the ~3% fall was re-confirmed), Delhi retail fuel prices, the Oil India royalty note, the ICRA Vedanta rationale, the PIB Samudra Manthan page (blocked) and the Petronet Q1 utilisation figure. HPCL and BPCL Q1 losses now follow Outlook Business (basis not stated), which differs from last week's consolidated figures. The IEA and OPEC October reports were not out yet. Asian Energy Services and IGL were left out because no source this week explained their specific exposure; May 2026 broker targets on ONGC were consulted but not used because they are dated. Source IDs skip S22, which was removed. Market-cap coverage runs from large caps (ONGC, Reliance, L&T, IOC, BPCL, GAIL) through mid caps (Oil India, Petronet, Welspun, HPCL, MGL, Gujarat Energy, Vedanta Oil & Gas) to small caps (Antelopus Selan, HOEC, Jindal Drilling, Deep Industries, Dolphin Offshore, SEAMEC, Maharashtra Seamless). No ratings or price targets are ours; broker targets are quoted as published.
